newsitem.title: COMOROS: Tourists, French doctors rush to help survivors.
newsitem.headline: Tourists, French doctors rush to help survivors.

text.p: Tourists at a luxury hotel in these Indian Ocean islands rushed to join the rescue effort when a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane crashed into the sea just off their swimming beach.
At least 45 of the 175 passengers and crew aboard survived against all odds.
"The plane skimmed the ground, went over the Galawa hotel and then it made too much smoke over the hotel swimming pool, made a big noise and crashed," one witness told Reuters.

"We saw the aircraft going down and down and down towards the hotel just in front of the main beach and then fall into the water... The aircraft is broken into two pieces," said Frederick Chretien, another witness.

Chretien, the manager of the Hotel Le Galawa in the Comoros, told BBC World Service radio by telephone that a group of 20 French doctors on holiday on the island were helping treat survivors in a nearby hospital.
The Boeing 767 broke into two pieces on impact about 500 metres (yards) from the shore. Parts of the fuselage floated.
Ethiopian Airlines officials said the plane crashed after apparently running out of fuel.
Local villagers and foreign tourists at the five-star hotel led rescue services before emergency services arrived.
Bodies retrieved from the sea were laid out in the conference room at the hotel.
"I saw 30 bodies...Mostly they are Asians and Africans. They were just covered with blankets," a Reuters correspondent on the scene said.
The Galawa is 40 km (25 miles) north of Moroni, the Comoran capital, and the hotel is owned by a South African company.
State radio appealed to all doctors to report immediately to the two main hospitals on Grande Comore, the island where Moroni is situated.
Chretien said one of the survivors had spoken of seeing two hijackers on board the plane.
The plane was hijacked on Saturday morning soon after it took off from Addis Ababa on a scheduled flight -- number ET 961 -- to Abidjan via Nairobi, Brazzaville and Lagos.
